artifact_sha256_reason: The Windows per-user NSIS installer built from the recorded commit (fc73386, the merge of pull request #223): 354229356 bytes, signed false. The digest was measured from the produced bytes, and the build's own measurement records it three ways -- the installer's sha256, the frozen backend tree's canonical listing, and the copy the installer carries at resources/backend/labcairn, which measured the same tree digest, so the installer carries that freeze byte for byte. The companion record docs/releases/v0.1.0-artifact.json carries the build's commands, the toolchain versions and the evidence. One thing is not settled by that build and is the owner's call: the installer's own file name and product version line still read 0.0.3, because shell/package.json was not bumped for this workbench release. The bytes carry this tree's product code; the name does not yet say so.

compatibility.data: SQLite store schema of migrations 0001-0030 (linear chain, head 0030_rule_sharing). v0.1.0 reads and writes the schema those revisions build; a workspace created by it migrates forward through the same chain, and rolling back the application without downgrading the database is the supported path (see rollback). No data migration compresses or rewrites existing rows: 0025-0030 add indexes, tables and columns for the Phase 4 features (revision-trajectory index, PPT index, model-suggestion runs, meeting index, pilot issue records, rule-sharing scope) and leave earlier rows readable.
compatibility.api: FastAPI routes on the single APIRouter mounted by src/labcairn/api/app.py (no path prefix), 58 endpoints measured at the recorded commit: the review/delivery, recovery, quality, roles, rule-sharing, issues, trajectory, PPT, meeting and pilot routes. The count is the 58 route decorators in src/labcairn/api/routes.py, the only file under src/labcairn/api/ that declares a route, and it is the number the app's own OpenAPI document carries as operations over 57 paths. These are the same paths tests/test_api.py exercises; the web package and the CLI talk to this surface only.

added: Delivery loop closed end to end: a paper goes from ingestion through claims extraction, staged analysis, report and figure generation to revision and restart recovery, exercised by the repository's own quickstart walk (docs/QUICKSTART.md).
Multi-source index: the paper revision trajectory (migration 0025), slide decks (0026) and meeting text (0028) are indexed alongside the document store, searchable from the API and the CLI workbench.

Rule sharing (Phase 4 section 8.5 / P4-G3): a mentor can confirm a distilled rule and share it with the group under a per-rule sharing scope (migration 0030), with the confirm/publish surface on the API and the workbench.

Pilot preparation: the LC-P4-PILOT runbook, desensitisation checklist, model-authorisation record (signed by the owner on 2026-11-24) and feedback-form template are in the tree, with the owner-decisions form (docs/plans/LC-P4-PILOT-owner-decisions.md) carrying the three section-12 decisions confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-24.
Pilot issue records (migration 0029): issues found in a trial round are recorded against the run and surfaced through the trajectory issue-key routes.
Model-suggestion runs (migration 0027) and the recovery/quality API routes (window G): recovery approvals and round-level quality/evidence checks are reachable from the API surface.
Workbench UI: the ingestion and quality report views, the pilot's issue record and the rule-sharing door are on the web workbench (windows of batches five and six).
Structured release records: scripts/release_record.py writes and checks the seven-element JSON record this file is one of (Phase 4 section 10).
fixed: Dual-head migration hazard: migrations 0024-0030 keep the revision chain linear (each revision's down_revision points at exactly one predecessor; no branch heads), so alembic upgrade has one path and a frozen revision cannot import a later one's state.

Layer boundaries: the application layer does not leak store types across the boundary; the trajectory layer is re-exported at a single seam (commit 3750040) so the API and CLI surfaces share one implementation.
Anchor drift: position anchors survive the revision/apply cycle without drifting, and the anchor registry (migration 0007) remains the single source of locator truth.

Type fidelity across the merge seams: the sixth batch's merge surfaced drift in the rule-sharing test helpers and the CLI ingest witnesses; both are typed for mypy --strict now (commits 033909f, 6066e01).
Crash-recovery matrix: the interrupted-write and interrupted-rewrite paths (drills) are witnessed to leave the store reconcilable, including the windows where a crash lands between write and confirm.
known_limits: The real-model authorisation record was filled from the owner's 2026-11-24 choices and signed the same day, so its status is AUTHORISED rather than DRAFT: the signature in docs/plans/LC-P4-PILOT-model-authorisation-draft.md §9 is what a real request runs against, and only inside the provider, material, budget, timeout and stop boundaries that record's §1-§7 state. The desensitisation checklist and the feedback-form template remain DRAFT.
The trial exit gate is PENDING: the real trial has not run; P4-G4 closes on participants' completed round and the triaged issue ledger.

The first release record's version v0.1.0 and date 2026-11-24 are confirmed by the owner; this record is re-anchored to the merged Phase 4 tree on main (fc73386, the merge of pull request #223), and every number in it was measured at that commit.

The web workbench ships as a development build served by the repository's own tooling; a Windows per-user installer was built and measured from this tree (see artifact_sha256 and docs/releases/v0.1.0-artifact.json), but it is unsigned, and its own file name and product version line still read 0.0.3 because the shell's package manifest was not bumped for this release -- the owner's call.

Substitute fallback is labelled substitute-model; a real-model call is gated by the signed authorisation record's recorded boundaries rather than by an unfilled field, and a request outside them stays refused.
rollback: Roll the application back by checking out the pre-release commit on main (16df3db04ef645212d303e5a4bd1817a8cd3fbbb, the commit main carried before the Phase 4 batch merge and the first parent of this record's commit fc73386) and reinstalling from that tree; the SQLite workspace needs no downgrade because migrations 0025-0030 only add tables, columns and indexes that an older application ignores. If a downgrade is required anyway, run alembic downgrade through the chain from 0030_rule_sharing back to the pinned base revision (0001) on a copy of the workspace database first -- never on the only copy -- and verify the result with tests/test_store_migrations.py before touching the original.
